A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GigaHands and retain the same dataset and acquisition pipeline. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original dataset analyses and experiments on motion synthesis, captioning, reconstruction, and tracking, including quantitative appendix results.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative cross-dataset transfer and hand-object interaction experiments.

M1.justification: The acquisition and tracking methods remain unchanged. Supplementary Section 6 adds MDM adaptations conditioned on text plus object trajectories for motion fulfillment, and on past hand/object poses for forecasting. T2M-GPT, promoted to the main synthesis backbone, was already evaluated in v1.

E1.justification: V3 adds two substantial task extensions: generating hand motions consistent with specified object trajectories and text, and jointly forecasting future hand/object poses. The underlying datasets remain the same; ARCTIC captioning examples were already present in v1.

E2.justification: The backbone comparison retains MDM, TM2T, and T2M-GPT. TACO and OakInk2 remain the comparison datasets and are reused in the added applications. InterDiff is cited for forecasting evaluation, without an evaluated comparator row.

E3.justification: The main synthesis comparison and scaling study switch from TM2T to T2M-GPT. New transfer evaluations use test-dataset feature extractors and refine TACO captions with ChatGPT-4o while selecting the best-performing generation per triplet. Forecasting introduces 10 observed/10 predicted frames and hand-joint, object-translation, and rotation errors.

E4.justification: V3 adds a three-by-three cross-dataset FID/Diversity analysis testing transfer among GigaHands, OakInk2, and TACO (supplementary Table 5). Synthesis scaling and representation/text-augmentation analyses are also revised. Existing captioning and tracking analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 evaluations and 95% confidence intervals for synthesis backbone and ablation comparisons. The added motion-fulfillment table uses the existing mean-of-20 practice; no new seed reporting, uncertainty-estimation method, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Synthesis scores are extensively revised: T2M-GPT's reported R@1/FID changes from 43.8%/3.37 in v1 Table 7 to 31.2%/4.70 in v3 supplementary Table 3. Transfer and hand-object tables add results. Main Table 2 also changes backbone, so its replacements cannot establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The contrastive loss, metric equations (supplementary Equations 1–5), and existing motion-representation definitions are substantively unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central dataset-scale, diversity, acquisition, and application claims remain. A limited applicability claim is reframed: the conclusion replaces 'in-the-wild data' with 'other data,' and the corresponding captioning heading changes to unlabeled datasets.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations of transfer difficulties caused by coarse TACO annotations and OakInk2's material/texture-based object descriptions. It also discusses rapid motion variation as a forecasting challenge and explicitly links verb diversity to pose/motion diversity. Existing studio-space and articulated/non-rigid tracking limitations remain.

D1.justification: The implementation section replaces TM2T-specific settings and its code reference with detailed T2M-GPT architecture, AdamW parameters, batch sizes, and training schedules. These newly document a previously evaluated backbone; acquisition, tracking, and annotation instructions largely persist.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations for residual networks, AdamW, the Transformer, and InterDiff to support implementation and forecasting evaluation. The broader positioning against existing hand datasets remains stable; references moved into the separate supplementary bibliography are retained.

P1.justification: V3 adds a supplementary contents page and separate numbering/bibliography, rewrites the synthesis implementation description, and makes localized terminology and generalization-language edits. Most existing prose and the overall section order remain.

P2.justification: V3 adds three result tables (supplementary Tables 5, 8, and 9), updates Figure 6's scaling plots, and changes table formatting and placement. Existing qualitative examples, acquisition diagrams, and tracking figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens validation through quantitative transfer tests and two hand-object tasks, while documenting T2M-GPT more fully. These gains are limited by best-generation selection in the TACO transfer test and an unexplained GigaHands FID difference: 4.70 in main Table 2/supplementary Table 3 versus 6.61 in supplementary Table 5. The additions support a modest overall improvement.
